Stillness keeping whole the truth of things (全物之真), agitation violating their nature (犯物之性), and only purity and stillness attaining the great things above (乃得如上諸大) carry the whole paraphrase; the chapter’s great things are his 如上諸大, the five great things of the chapter. Plain sense matches Legge’s chapter (great achievements thought poor, fulness deemed a void, straight deemed crooked, art seeming stupid) and says what the closing line does without a four-word run from it. verse.js ok (Tao Te Ching 45, at [44]); entry-check ok. Minor note only: “agitation” renders the 躁 that Legge prints as constant action in the sentence before the key verse, which is Wang Bi’s own term, not drift.
